title: Sell Mineral Rights in Custer, MT
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Custer, MT
metaDescription: Custer sits along the Yellowstone River in Yellowstone County. A retired E&P engineer explains title basics and honest development expectations for this small river community.
heroLead: Custer is a small Yellowstone River community, and I treat any mineral interest here the same way I would elsewhere in the county: check the actual records before saying anything about value.
intro: Sitting along the Yellowstone River, downstream from Billings, Custer is a small unincorporated community in a county whose mineral development has historically concentrated far more heavily in refining and pipeline infrastructure than in upstream drilling near this stretch of the river.

sections.heading: River Valley Farmland Title
paragraphs: Land around Custer follows the same general pattern as much of the Yellowstone Valley: homestead-era settlement, agricultural use ever since, and mineral rights that were frequently severed at some point but rarely developed. Confirming your recorded interest against the county's title records is the necessary starting point before anything else.

sections.heading: What's Actually Happening Underground
paragraphs: I check current permit and lease activity for the Custer area specifically, and historically that's turned up little to nothing. This is a farming and ranching community along a working river valley, not a zone of active oil and gas exploration.

sections.heading: An Honest Number
paragraphs: For most interests near Custer, I'd expect a modest value reflecting the absence of current development, built off comparable undeveloped tracts elsewhere in Yellowstone County rather than any speculation about future activity that isn't currently supported by permits.

I'd also ask whether the tract has ever changed hands as part of a larger ranch sale, since surface and mineral estates sometimes get separated at that point without either party fully realizing it. A quick courthouse check settles the question either way.

faqs.question: Is there oil and gas drilling near Custer, MT?
faqs.answer: Little to none based on current permit records. This is a farming and ranching community along the Yellowstone River without significant development history.

faqs.question: Where do I check my mineral title near Custer?
faqs.answer: The Yellowstone County Clerk and Recorder in Billings holds the recorded deeds for Custer and the surrounding area.

faqs.question: Should I expect a high offer for undeveloped minerals near Custer?
faqs.answer: I'd give you an honest, modest range reflecting the lack of current activity rather than an inflated figure that doesn't match the area's actual development history.

faqs.question: Could a past ranch sale near Custer have separated my minerals from the surface without my family knowing?
faqs.answer: It happens more often than people expect, particularly on older ranch transactions where the seller quietly reserved minerals. A courthouse title search will show whether that occurred on your specific tract.
